subject: HealthNova retention scope + BYOK clarification
messages:
From: Procurement <procurement@healthnova.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Security Team <security@healthnova.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data retention windows + KMS ownership question

Hi Naomi / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re moving this through a short internal review and have two constraints we need clarified before procurement can advance:

1) Retention: We need a firm commitment that conversational logs and embeddings tied to PII will be purged within 45 days by default, with a 90‑day option for audit data only. Can you confirm how Redwood maps data types to retention buckets and whether manual carveouts are possible?

2) KMS / BYOK: HealthNova requires control of customer master keys for any production dataset containing PHI. Is Redwood able to support BYOK for dedicated/private deployments and what’s the exception path for Hosted API pilots?

We’d appreciate a short summary and any evidence artifacts (audit log sample, retention matrix) you can share.

Thanks —
Maya Reed
Procurement, HealthNova
procurement@healthnova.com

Folks — looping you in to triage HealthNova’s asks (see below). They want a quick summary for procurement and some evidence. I’m putting the key asks here so we can align on what to send back.

Ask summary from HealthNova:
- Default purge window for conversational logs/PII: 45 days (with an opt‑in 90d audit window)
- Ability to BYOK for production workloads containing PHI; clarity on Hosted API exception path
- Evidence: sample audit logs, retention mapping matrix, SSO/KMS architecture diagram

Proposed internal owners:
- Marissa: product/behavior on retention buckets + what’s configurable via Console/API
- Karthik: KMS/BYOK feasibility, exception gating, and evidence we can provide
- Ben/Grace: operational side (audit logs, timeframe to collect evidence, legal gating)

Quick notes: we have an existing retention matrix but it’s not HealthNova‑tuned; I attached a working draft (retention-scope-matrix-v1.xlsx) and a short summary doc (sso-kms-exceptions-summary.pdf). Please review and reply with:
1) What we can commit to in writing (for procurement) vs recommended configuration for Dedicated/Private
2) Exact evidence artifacts we can share now vs require redaction/legal review
3) Any blockers or timeline (EOD Monday?)

Thanks — I’ll consolidate and send back a short one‑page to HealthNova.

— Naomi

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:31:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Data retention windows + KMS ownership question

Thanks Naomi — reviewed the draft matrix and made product notes inline. High level position from product:

- Retention mapping: We can map artifacts into three buckets (session conversational logs, embeddings, and audit traces). Default platform retention is configurable per account: 30/60/90/365 days. For HealthNova’s ask we can commit to a default 45d purge for session logs (we’ll implement a 45d preset and label it in Console). Embeddings retained separately — recommend 90d limit for embeddings tied to profiles with opt‑out for analytics.

- Manual carveouts: yes — account admins can request temporary evidence carveouts; these require an approval ticket and automated hold flag. For procurement language we should call this a "time‑boxed evidence hold" with a maximum 90d extension and audit trace that shows the hold window.

- Hosted API pilots: Hosted cannot BYOK today for shared tenancy. We can offer an exception path: pilot customers can use dedicated tokens with ephemeral-encryption-at-rest (no BYOK) plus contractual controls and stricter audit sampling. For production PHI we must recommend Dedicated or Private with BYOK.

Actionable items I suggest we include in the reply:
1) A one‑pager commitment (45d default for session logs; 90d for embeddings audit)
2) A short note on BYOK: Supported for Dedicated/Private; Hosted pilot exception path explained
3) Evidence we can attach today: redacted audit log sample + retention matrix + architecture sketch (no keys/materials). Anything else needs security/legal review (2–3 business days).

I can draft the one‑pager this morning.

— Marissa
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@healthnova.com>, Security Team <security@healthnova.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Data retention windows + KMS ownership question

Quick security triage —

1) BYOK constraints: For Dedicated/Private we support customer KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) with CMK rotation and HSM‑backed roots. Requirements for BYOK: (a) dedicated tenancy, (b) key escrow policy agreed, (c) documented key rotation schedule, (d) monitoring hooks enabled. We can produce a short control table for procurement to sign off.

2) Hosted exceptions: We cannot provide full BYOK for Hosted. Exception path: 30‑day pilot SLA with contractual encryption-in-transit and envelope keys under Redwood control, plus mandatory logging and periodic evidence snapshots. This is a commercial/legal exception and requires approval from Security and Legal.

3) Evidence artifacts: we can share the following immediately (redacted): a) sample audit log lines (redacted IDs) b) retention mapping (the attached matrix) c) SAML metadata diagram (no secrets). Anything showing key material or internal key ids requires redaction & legal signoff.

4) Request: Naomi — please confirm if we should present the Hosted pilot exception as: (A) conditional technical pilot (30d, no BYOK) or (B) postpone pilot until Dedicated is provisioned. Procurement will want option A recorded in the MSA if they proceed. If they insist on BYOK for pilot we need legal approval and it will push timelines.

cc: Ben — can Ops produce the redacted audit sample by EOD Tuesday? Grace — can you confirm the timeline for evidence collection + any cost impact for a time‑boxed hold?

— Karthik
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
